target: 秀支替戾岡，僕谷劬禿當
purpose: Audit every proposed Yeniseian morpheme against Werner 2005 and recent scholarship, separating direct Arin attestations, family-level structural parallels, reconstructions, and unresolved gaps.

sources.citation: Heinrich Werner, Die Jenissej-Sprachen des 18. Jahrhunderts (2005)

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner 2005: Arin H kel = Heer/army; kelbaxal'a = I make war; keln'a keko = warrior.
No independent Werner Arin lexical element identified that explains the initial syllable of the reconstructed śuke.
morphemes.cost: One Chinese syllabic position remains without a securely independently attested Arin morpheme.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner independently documents rich Yeniseian directional/version morphology and Ket paradigms meaning come out/go away, but this audit has not identified a direct Arin t- = out morpheme.
morphemes.cost: Semantic slot is plausible in the family template, exact segment-to-function identity remains reconstructed.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner's Ket come-out paradigm inserts l in past forms; Yugh paradigms independently show ir/r in past forms. This verifies a family-level liquid past slot independent of the couplet.
morphemes.cost: Direct Old Arin past morphology is poorly attested, so branch-specific identity is not established.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner directly records Arin go forms unkut / baxatum, Pumpokol bulün/bulun, and Ket/Yugh forms of the boyat/bodde type; no direct Arin or secure Pumpokol ek = go entry was identified.
morphemes.cost: Requires deeper Proto-Yeniseian/root reconstruction rather than direct Arin lexical confirmation.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner reconstructs Arin animate 3PL predicative -an/-ian and documents -an-like plural subject material across Ket/Yugh paradigms.
morphemes.cost: Person-number realization differs across branches and Werner warns Arin paradigm coverage is sparse.

morphemes.primary_evidence: The Yeniseian analysis largely preserves this as an opaque title/name slot rather than deriving it from independently attested Yeniseian morphology.
morphemes.cost: 谷 is additionally polyphonic and remains a latent K/L/Y transcription state.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner's direct Arin foot forms are apil/pil; Pumpokol foot is anin; Ket/Yugh foot forms are bul-type. No direct got = foot entry is independently attested in Werner 2005.
morphemes.cost: The analysis depends on deeper comparative reconstruction and/or a Ket incorporated body-part lineage rather than direct Arin evidence.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner independently documents rigid Yeniseian actant slots and 3SG masculine a/o-type actant forms in Ket; transitive paradigms distinguish object person/class in fixed positions.
morphemes.cost: This verifies the structural type, not the exact Old Arin surface o in this verb.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Werner's direct Arin take is menkamen (and bulabmenkamen = take away); Ket/Imbak take uses kaj-/kam- type material. Vovin's kt is therefore reconstructive, not a direct Arin dictionary match.
morphemes.cost: No independently attested Old Arin kt = take form has been established in the primary dictionary.

morphemes.primary_evidence: Same family-level -an/-ian support as in the first predicate.

Werner has a peculiar Arin stand paradigm with 3PL -tan, but the same surface -tan is also 1PL and Werner's general animate 3PL is -an/-ian. Vovin's segmentation assigns t to root kt plus -aŋ, while Bonmann & Fries discuss surface <taŋ> as an Arin 3PL ending.
morphemes.cost: The same surface t cannot simultaneously be counted as independent support for both root kt and suffix -taŋ without an explicit segmentation model.

global_findings.finding: Complex templatic verb morphology with fixed actant, tense/aspect, directional/incorporative and root positions is independently documented in Werner; this strongly supports the typological plausibility of a multi-morpheme Yeniseian parse.
Werner repeatedly warns that Arin grammatical data are sparse and complete paradigms often require analogy with better-attested Yeniseian languages.
Werner says only two or three secure Pumpokol verbal forms with B-affixes are attested and no broad conclusions about Pumpokol verbal inflection can be drawn.

Werner explicitly separates genuine Pumpokol Müller material from later Yugh forms mislabelled as Pumpokol; kasna 'take' belongs to the contaminated/mislabelled side and cannot be used as secure Pumpokol evidence.

Within the couplet itself the strongest primary Arin anchor is kel 'army' after gloss reveal; the strongest blind support is the family-level templatic morphology, not any single uniquely Arin suffix.

The second predicate remains the weakest lexical portion: got 'foot(?)' and kt 'take' are not directly verified by Werner's Arin lexicon, while object/subject slot structure is independently plausible.

model_implication.old_view: Old Arin had a modest blind lead driven by repeated -aŋ and a surface -taŋ argument.
model_implication.new_view: Old Arin remains plausible, but the evidence should be decomposed: direct Arin lexical kel is strong only after gloss reveal; blind evidence comes mainly from Yeniseian template/past/object/subject architecture; ek, got and kt remain reconstruction-heavy gaps.
model_implication.next_highest_IG: Audit Proto-Yeniseian etymological dictionaries / Fortescue-Vajda for ek 'go', got 'foot', kt 'take', and t 'out' before increasing Old Arin confidence.
